Lesson No. 227: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 1 to 8

The disjointed letters (huruf muqatta'at) have been discussed in several surahs. This repeated opening, "Ha Mim," carries the same indication. The Qur'an follows the practice of repeatedly pointing to realities that affect the human heart and mind, and repetition is needed because a human being constantly needs reminding. As years pass, the goal fades from human sight, and to fix any conscious truth in the mind a person needs repeated admonition. The One who revealed the Qur'an knows the fitrah (innate nature) He created very well. He is the One who gave humans their qualities and capacities, so He reminds them again and again. He is the Creator of hearts and the Turner of hearts.

"Ha Mim... Ar-Rahim" (41:1–2): "A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." Ha Mim serves as the name of the surah, or as the genus of the Qur'an, which is formed from these very letters. Ha Mim is the subject (mubtada') and "tanzil" (revelation) is the predicate (khabar). That is, these are the Ha Mim (from which the Qur'an is made), which is being sent down by the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The mention of the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful at the time of the revelation of the Book means that the exalted attribute of this revelation is the mercy of God. This Book and what it contains came as a mercy to the worlds (rahmatan lil-'alamin). It is not a mercy only for those who believe and obey it, but also for others. It is a mercy not only for humankind but for all living beings, because this Book gave the world a way of life which affected the whole world. Humanity received new life. It gave concepts to humanity, gave it knowledge, and in short, this Qur'an completely changed the direction in which humanity was moving. The merciful effects of the Qur'an were not confined to the people of faith; its effects were global, and from that time until today these effects continue. Those who study human history with justice, examine it from a general human perspective, and encompass human activities fully in that study, find this reality and are satisfied with this point: that the Qur'an is a mercy to the worlds. Some fair-minded people have acknowledged this and put it on record.

"A Book whose verses are elaborated, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who have knowledge" (41:3): That is, its verses have been made detailed and firmly structured according to purposes and aims, according to the natures of people, according to societies and eras, and according to people's psychology and needs. This is the distinctive feature of this Book; from this perspective the Book is detailed (mufassal) and firm (muhkam). In all these aspects this Book is detailed. Then it is in Arabic.

"For a people who have knowledge" (li-qawmin ya'lamun, 41:3): That is, those who have the capacity for knowledge can understand and distinguish the genuine from the counterfeit. The great purpose of the revelation of this Qur'an is good news and warning.

"A bringer of good news and a warner" (bashiran wa nadhiran, 41:4): This Qur'an gives good news to the believers and warns the deniers and evildoers. It also tells the causes of good news and warning. It tells these in a clear Arabic, and it is presented to those who are Arabs, yet most of them do not accept it.

"But most of them turned away, and they do not listen" (41:4): And these people turned away and did not listen, and by turning away they shielded their hearts from hearing the Qur'an. Because the Qur'an has a powerful effect, those who led the common masses told them not to listen, as its details will come later.

"And those who disbelieve say: Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation, that perhaps you may overcome" (41:26): At times they did hear, but in a manner as though they did not hear, and because of their obstinacy they resisted the effects the Qur'an had upon them. In effect, they are deaf; they do not truly hear.

"And they say: Our hearts are under coverings against that to which you call us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier, so act, we are acting" (41:5): They said this out of deep obstinacy and enmity, and they said it to disappoint the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that he would stop calling people, because they themselves felt the influence of his call in their own hearts, and they were firmly determined in the position that they would never believe.

So they said that their hearts were covered with coverings, that your words do not reach our hearts; that there is plugging in our ears, so your words do not reach us; that there are veils between you and us, so there is no way left for contact. Therefore leave us to our condition; we do not care what you do, what you say, whom you fear, or whom you promise. We will walk our own path. If you wish, walk your path, do whatever you want. We will not listen. Bring on the punishment with which you threaten us; we do not care.

These were the conditions and difficulties which the first caller, ﷺ, faced. Yet despite this, he continued calling people and never stopped. He was never affected by these disheartening circumstances; he never thought that so much time had passed and God's promise had not been fulfilled and punishment had not come upon the enemies. He would simply say that the fulfilment of God's promise was not in his power. He was only a human being. God's message comes to him and he conveys it, calls people to the One God, and tells those who accept to remain firm on this path, and warns the polytheists of an evil end. What follows in later stages is not in his control. He is only a human being and one commissioned.

"Say: I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is only one God, so take the straight course toward Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to the polytheists" (41:6): How great is this patience! How great is this forbearance! What a great faith and submission and contentment! But only that caller can understand such a situation, only he can bear such conditions with patience, only he can advance in such circumstances calling people while indifferent to the environment, and endure turning away, denial, arrogance, and insulting treatment, who has passed through such conditions, who has tested that haste must not be done, who has resisted the turning-away, arrogant, and rebellious, who has borne hardship in the path of the call, and who has found the resolve to bear hardship in the path of the call and then stood firm despite these difficulties.

It is because of such situations that the prophets and messengers were repeatedly instructed to be patient, for the path of the call is the path of patience. Long patience, and the trial of patience, first appear in the desire, which is very intense, that the call should succeed quickly, that victory should come soon, even if there are no signs of victory; yet the caller continues working with patience, steadfastness, and submission. And in response to these difficulties, turning-away, and arrogance and heedlessness, the Messenger of Allah only says:

"And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakah and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter" (41:6–7): There may be some relevance in mentioning zakah here, though no narration mentions it; this verse is Meccan, and zakah became obligatory in Medina in the second year after the Hijrah. Although in principle zakah was known in Makkah as well, in Medina it became obligatory together with a fixed nisab, and a defined obligation began to be collected. In Makkah it was a general practice; people gave zakah voluntarily, there was no fixed limit, and payment was left to the conscience of the giver. Ultimately, disbelief is that disbelief which, as a result, makes a person deserving of eternal ruin. Some have interpreted zakah in this verse as meaning faith and purification from shirk. This meaning also cannot be rejected, and in such circumstances this possibility certainly exists.

Now the caller of truth, to show them how great a crime they commit by committing disbelief and polytheism, takes these people on a tour of this universe: just consider this vast cosmos comprising the heavens and the earth, and how small and weak you are in comparison. This tour is given so that they may also see the sovereignty of Allah which they deny, because the human being too is an extremely insignificant part of the nature of the universe. And so that they may tell them that you are looking at this call from an extremely narrow viewpoint; you can only see that "there is none like me" (hamcho mādīgar nīst). You look only at yourselves and at the person of Muhammad ﷺ, and you think that if you accept Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah, he will attain a lofty position. This narrow-mindedness prevents you from seeing the great truth which Muhammad ﷺ has brought, whose details are recorded in the Holy Qur'an. This truth is connected with the heavens, the earth, humankind, the whole of human history, and that great truth which lies beyond time and place, and which has been placed in the design of this universe:

This is the distinctive feature of this Book; from this perspective the Book is detailed (mufassal) and firm (muhkam). In all these aspects this Book is detailed. Then it is in Arabic.

"For a people who have knowledge" (li-qawmin ya'lamun, 41:3): That is, those who have the capacity for knowledge can understand and distinguish the genuine from the counterfeit. The great purpose of the revelation of this Qur'an is good news and warning.

"A bringer of good news and a warner" (bashiran wa nadhiran, 41:4): This Qur'an gives good news to the believers and warns the deniers and evildoers. It also tells the causes of good news and warning. It tells these in a clear Arabic, and it is presented to those who are Arabs, yet most of them do not accept it.

"But most of them turned away, and they do not listen" (41:4): And these people turned away and did not listen, and by turning away they shielded their hearts from hearing the Qur'an. Because the Qur'an has a powerful effect, those who led the common masses told them not to listen, as its details will come later.

"And those who disbelieve say: Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation, that perhaps you may overcome" (41:26): At times they did hear, but in a manner as though they did not hear, and because of their obstinacy they resisted the effects the Qur'an had upon them. In effect, they are deaf; they do not truly hear.

"And they say: Our hearts are under coverings against that to which you call us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier, so act, we are acting" (41:5): They said this out of deep obstinacy and enmity, and they said it to disappoint the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that he would stop calling people, because they themselves felt the influence of his call in their own hearts, and they were firmly determined in the position that they would never believe.

So they said that their hearts were covered with coverings, that your words do not reach our hearts; that there is plugging in our ears, so your words do not reach us; that there are veils between you and us, so there is no way left for contact. Therefore leave us to our condition; we do not care what you do, what you say, whom you fear, or whom you promise. We will walk our own path. If you wish, walk your path, do whatever you want. We will not listen. Bring on the punishment with which you threaten us; we do not care.

These were the conditions and difficulties which the first caller, ﷺ, faced. Yet despite this, he continued calling people and never stopped. He was never affected by these disheartening circumstances; he never thought that so much time had passed and God's promise had not been fulfilled and punishment had not come upon the enemies. He would simply say that the fulfilment of God's promise was not in his power. He was only a human being. God's message comes to him and he conveys it, calls people to the One God, and tells those who accept to remain firm on this path, and warns the polytheists of an evil end. What follows in later stages is not in his control. He is only a human being and one commissioned.

"Say: I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is only one God, so take the straight course toward Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to the polytheists" (41:6): How great is this patience! How great is this forbearance! What a great faith and submission and contentment! But only that caller can understand such a situation, only he can bear such conditions with patience, only he can advance in such circumstances calling people while indifferent to the environment, and endure turning away, denial, arrogance, and insulting treatment, who has passed through such conditions, who has tested that haste must not be done, who has resisted the turning-away, arrogant, and rebellious, who has borne hardship in the path of the call, and who has found the resolve to bear hardship in the path of the call and then stood firm despite these difficulties.

It is because of such situations that the prophets and messengers were repeatedly instructed to be patient, for the path of the call is the path of patience. Long patience, and the trial of patience, first appear in the desire, which is very intense, that the call should succeed quickly, that victory should come soon, even if there are no signs of victory; yet the caller continues working with patience, steadfastness, and submission. And in response to these difficulties, turning-away, and arrogance and heedlessness, the Messenger of Allah only says:

"And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakah and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter" (41:6–7): There may be some relevance in mentioning zakah here, though no narration mentions it; this verse is Meccan, and zakah became obligatory in Medina in the second year after the Hijrah. Although in principle zakah was known in Makkah as well, in Medina it became obligatory together with a fixed nisab, and a defined obligation began to be collected. In Makkah it was a general practice; people gave zakah voluntarily, there was no fixed limit, and payment was left to the conscience of the giver. Ultimately, disbelief is that disbelief which, as a result, makes a person deserving of eternal ruin. Some have interpreted zakah in this verse as meaning faith and purification from shirk. This meaning also cannot be rejected, and in such circumstances this possibility certainly exists.

Now the caller of truth, to show them how great a crime they commit by committing disbelief and polytheism, takes these people on a tour of this universe: just consider this vast cosmos comprising the heavens and the earth, and how small and weak you are in comparison. This tour is given so that they may also see the sovereignty of Allah which they deny, because the human being too is an extremely insignificant part of the nature of the universe. And so that they may tell them that you are looking at this call from an extremely narrow viewpoint; you can only see that "there is none like me" (hamcho mādīgar nīst). You look only at yourselves and at the person of Muhammad ﷺ, and you think that if you accept Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah, he will attain a lofty position. This narrow-mindedness prevents you from seeing the great truth which Muhammad ﷺ has brought, whose details are recorded in the Holy Qur'an. This truth is connected with the heavens, the earth, humankind, the whole of human history, and that great truth which lies beyond time and place, and which has been placed in the design of this universe:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verses 9–12 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 9 to 12

O Prophet, say to them: when you disbelieve and, in your carelessness, utter this great statement, you commit a very great crime; this is an extremely ugly and disliked act. You deny the One who created the earth, placed mountains within it, put blessings in it, and set within this earth every requirement for sustenance in full measure; who created the heavens and completed all these works in four days, and supplied the needs of all who ask. He who created the heavens, ordered them, and especially adorned the nearest heaven to the world with splendor. The earth and the heavens bowed their heads before His laws of power and His commands. Yet you, O people of the earth, deny and act arrogantly.

But the wording of the Qur'an, in accordance with the Qur'anic style of expression, presents these themes in a manner that the matter immediately enters the heart and shakes it to its core. Read again the words of this Qur'an and reflect.

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? He is the Lord of the worlds. He set firm mountains upon it from above, put blessings in it, and provided within it sustenance for all who ask, in due measure, in the right way. All this was accomplished in four days.﴾ (41:9–10)

Here it is said that the earth was created in two days. Before further discussion of the creation of the earth, a comment is made to negate association with Him and it is stated:

﴿That is the Lord of the worlds﴾ (41:9). You deny this Lord and associate others with Him, though the earth on which you walk was created by Him. Therefore arrogance and carelessness do not befit you. This is a very ugly act. After this, the rest of the matter follows.

The question is: which are these two days in which the earth was created, and in which the mountains were set and life was put into the earth, so that these become four days?

These days are in fact the Days of Allah, and only Allah knows their length. These days are certainly not the days of this earth, because the days of the earth are the temporal measure that came into existence after the earth was formed and its rotation was fixed. Just as there are days of this earth, which arise from its axial rotation and its annual revolution around the sun, so each of the celestial bodies has its own days. The stars have their own days, which differ from the days of the earth; some are shorter than the earth's days and some longer. The days in which the earth first came into being, then mountains were formed in it, then sustenance and necessities were placed in it according to need, were some other days, and their measure was also different. We do not have knowledge of this, but we do know with certainty that these days were very much longer than those two.

According to what human knowledge has reached until today, we can say that by this is meant the periods through which this earth passed until it settled in its present orbit, its crust hardened, and it became fit for the establishment of life, the life we know. According to the theories put forward until today, this took nine thousand million years of our earth's standard of days.

These are also scientific theories, compiled after the study of rocks and observations. In the study of the Qur'an we do not call these practical theories the final word, because they are not final. These are theories, and changes come in them. We cannot make the Qur'an subordinate to them. However, if there is closeness and agreement between these theories and the text of the Qur'an, we may say that this theory may be correct, and such a theory may also assist in the interpretation of the Qur'an, and through it we may draw near to the meaning of the Qur'an.

According to today's theories, the prevailing view is that the earth too was once a ball of fire, as the sun is now, and in the form of gas. This earth too was a part of the sun, which separated from it. Scientists do not agree on why or how this happened, but it took a long time for it to cool, while its core is still in the state where huge mountains melt and begin to boil.

"When the crust of the earth cooled, it became hard." At first it was hard rock, and there were layers of rock, upper and lower. In the very earliest period, vapours arose, of which two-thirds was hydrogen and one-third oxygen. Through their combination, water came into being upon the earth.

"Wind and water cooperated to break the rocks, cut them into pieces, lift them from one place and heap them up in another, and through this soil came into being, in which crops could grow. Thus wind and water broke the mountains, lowered high places, and performed the work of filling up hollows and low places. Therefore, in everything that exists or will exist within the earth, we see construction and destruction proceeding side by side."

"The upper part of the earth, which may be called its crust, remains in constant motion and change. When waves rise in the sea, this crust is affected. By the heat of the sun, the water of the sea turns to vapour, rises toward the heavens, takes the form of clouds, and sweet water falls upon the earth. Heavy rains fall, floods come, rivers flow, and these move over the crust of the earth and act upon it. They act upon a stone and rock in such a way that they transform it from one kind of rock into another. Then these floods and rivers carry it off and take it elsewhere, and after centuries the face of the earth changes again. After thousands and millions of years, vast transformations occur. Then ice forms upon the mountains, and it performs the same work that wind and water do. The sun too acts upon the crust of the earth in the same way that wind and water do; it heats it. Then living animals upon the earth also keep changing this face of the earth, and volcanic activity also produces changes on the earth."

"You may ask any geologist about the rocks of this earth; he will give you much information about rocks and will describe three major kinds of them, such as Igneous Rocks, which came out in the form of the molten material of the earth's core, which then cooled. He will present to you the lava rock (granite) as an example, and showing you the stone, he will tell you that within it are white, red and black shining materials. These are chemical compounds and have their own existence, since they are stones of mixed metals. He will tell you that the entire crust of the whole surface of the earth is made of these stones. When this earth was formed, long ago, rains began, rivers appeared upon the earth, or ice melted, storms blew, and the sun showed its effect. These influences caused breakdown and erosion within these igneous rocks. From their debris and the chemical material within them, these new rocks came into being, and from these lava rocks many other rocks of various colours and kinds came into being."

"Now there is another important kind of rock, which in the language of geology is called Sedimentary Rocks. These are rocks that were formed through the breakdown of the original hard rocks of the earth by the action of water, wind, sun, or living things. They are called Sedimentary because they are not in their original place. They break down from their original rocks and, through water, wind and storms, are transported to another place, where they gather in the form of sediment and harden."

"An example of these sedimentary rocks is the limestone from which the whole Muqattam mountain is made; the people of Cairo break stone from that mountain to build their houses. Experts will say that this is calcium carbonate, and that it was separated from the earth by living things or by chemical processes. Then sand too is made of stones of this kind, and calcium acid is also formed from this kind; it too has come out of other rocks, such as dry sedimentary stone and the stone of dried clay. All of these arise according to the earlier principle."

These are the original rocks from which the sedimentary rocks were formed, of various kinds. Thus it is understood that the original rocks are lava rocks. When the surface of the earth solidified and its molten state ended, and this happened very early, there was nothing on the surface of the earth but lava rock. Then vapours and water came into being and began to act upon the lava rock, breaking it down. Winds and various kinds of gases also acted in it. Fierce storms and the heat of the sun also gave assistance. All these stages came together and each acted according to its nature and temperament, and these changed into stones of lava. Now buildings are made from these stones, minerals are extracted, and most important of all, soil was extracted from this hard lava stone, which gathered at various places on the earth's surface, and this very soil became the cradle for plants and animals.

"Lava rocks are not useful for cultivation, crops and irrigation. But from them soft, smooth soil is produced, or this soil is gathered from other similar rocks, and from this soil plants and animals came into being. Thus the way was prepared for the creation of man, the chief of the creatures of this earth."

This long journey, whose revelation has been made by modern science, helps us understand that the days that were taken in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the four days taken in the creation of the earth, the placing of mountains upon it, and the arrangement of blessings and necessities within it, were the four Days of Allah, the length of which we do not know, nor do we know what measure or standard applies to them. Yet it is certain that they were not the days of this earth of ours.

Now we shall reflect upon each phrase of the Qur'anic text, before we leave the subject of the earth and turn toward the heavens:

﴿And He placed firm mountains upon it from above﴾ (41:10). Sometimes the word "rawasi" is also used for these mountains. Rawasi means anchored ships and mountains, and in some places mountains are called rawasi, on the basis of the phrase "an tameed bikum," "lest it sway with you" (16:15), meaning that the earth is anchored. These mountains fix it in one place, so that people do not slip away. There was a time when people thought that the earth was fixed in one place and rested on firm foundations. Now the time has come when this earth is a sphere, a small ball floating in space and supported by nothing. When people were first told this, they must have been bewildered, looking around them to see whether indeed they would fall or slip away, or whether they would be swept off into the depths of space. Be assured: Allah has held it up in space, and the earth and heavens cannot move or slip from their place. If their balance were ever disturbed, none but Allah could restore it. Be at peace! The laws of nature that Allah has set in the universe are very firm, and Allah is the Mighty, the Wise.

Further study of the mountains is needed. They have been called "rawasi" by Allah. They bind the earth so that it does not slip away, as we explained elsewhere in Zilal al-Quran: the depths within the seas and the heights upon the earth balance the two parts, so that the two portions of the earth, sea and land, are equalized.

Listen to a scientist:

"Whatever event occurs within the earth, or upon its surface, causes matter to be transferred from one place to another, and this affects its rotation. Tidal action is not the only factor, that is, regarding the decrease in the earth's speed; even the water that rivers carry from one place to another affects the speed of the earth. Winds that blow in a particular direction also have an effect. The shifting of the sea-floor level in places, and the rising of land surfaces from place to place, also affects the speed of the earth's rotation, and it is also a factor affecting the earth's rotational speed that the earth expands or contracts in some place, even if this contraction and expansion is limited to a few centimetres."

In short, this sensitive earth, whose sensitivity we have studied, is it so far-fetched that these towering mountains establish balance within its speed and prevent it from becoming unbalanced? This is why the Qur'an said fourteen hundred years ago: "an tameed bikum," "lest it sway with you."

﴿And He placed in it blessings, and determined in it its sustenance in due measure﴾ (41:10). This phrase must have conveyed to our predecessors the meaning that He made the crops grow and placed within the earth certain useful minerals and metals, such as gold, silver and iron. But today, the blessings of the earth which Allah has opened to man, and which were placed in this earth centuries ago, and from which we benefit, have made the meaning of this phrase very broad indeed.

Now we have seen how the elements of air cooperated and water was formed, and how water and air cooperated, and the sun and the winds cooperated, and the soil was formed and became fit for cultivation. And through the joint cooperation of water, sun and winds, rains fall; it is rain through which all water is supplied: through sweet canals, through rivers and streams, and through the reservoirs and springs within the earth. All these are blessings and provisions. And then air, and our respiratory system, and the bodies of all living creatures.

"The earth is a sphere and a ball. Over it is wrapped a layer of rock, and over the greater part of this layer of rock is a layer of water with which this rock is enveloped. Then above this water and rock layer is an atmospheric sphere which envelops the world in the form of a thick gas. This atmospheric sphere is like the sea. It has a depth like the sea. We humans, animals and plants live at the bottom of this ocean of air, and we live very comfortably."

"In the air we breathe, we take in oxygen; plants build their bodies from the air, taking carbon from the air, indeed taking carbon from carbon dioxide, which the people of chemistry call carbon dioxide. Plants build their bodies from the oxide of coal. We eat plants, and we also eat animals, and animals eat plants. Our bodies are formed from both. The air contains nitrogen; it makes the oxygen mild. Otherwise we would burn up the moment we breathe. Water vapours create moisture in the air. There are some other gases which are found in small quantities and are not fixed. Among them are helium, neon etc., and hydrogen gas; these have been present in the air since the initial creation."

The material which we eat and from which we benefit in our lives, although provision has a broader meaning than what only enters the stomach, all these things consist of that original material and elements which this earth holds in its belly or holds in the atmosphere. For example, what is sugar? It is a compound of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, and water is composed of hydrogen and oxygen. These two things are the major compounds of our food and drink. Moreover, clothing and tools are also made from those same elements which Allah has deposited within this earth.

These are the matters which point to the blessings of this earth and the sources of provision within it, which were made in four days, or four long periods, that is, the Days of Allah, the measure of which we do not know.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke. He said to it and to the earth: "Come into being, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly, as obedient ones." Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and revealed in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made it well protected. That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ (41:11–12)

The meaning of istiwa' here is to intend, and Allah's intention is that He directs His will towards it. Thumma (then) sometimes is not for chronological sequence but also comes for progressive meaning. Since heavens appear exalted and high to humans, the word thumma came for it.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke﴾ (41:11). It is said that before the creation of the stars there was a state like the state of "sadam", and it was a kind of gas, like smoke.

"In the sadam (Black Hole), the gas and dust that exists is the same that has survived the creation of stars. The theory of the creation of the universe is that the galaxy is composed of gas and dust. When this gas and dust became more dense, as a result stars came into being. Some debris remained; this remaining debris took the form of sadam. In this vast galaxy, the part that remains is dispersed, in the form of gas and dust. Its quantity is as much as the stars that have formed. These stars continually draw in that remaining gas and dust by their gravitational pull. Thus through this process the heavens are being cleaned, but the stars that absorb this dust are very few in that terrifying space, and the regions to be cleared of it are very vast." This may be correct, because it is closer to the meaning in this verse.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke﴾ (41:11), until He made them heavens, and in them two days of Allah were spent, that is, a long period. After this we shall now reflect on this reality.

﴿He said to it and to the earth: "Come into being, willingly or unwillingly."﴾ (41:11) This verse contains a wondrous allusion to the law of nature and the order of creation that has been set in this universe, and the relationship of this universe with its Creator is a relationship of obedience and submission. The entire universe moves according to the will and command of Allah. Only humans are a creature who, compelled before the order of Allah, bows in submission, and often this happens. This human too is certainly obedient to this order of nature; he cannot escape from it. He is an extremely minor component of this great universe, and the universal laws of this universe apply to him too, whether he is pleased or not. But in this universe, this human is the only noble being who does not obey Allah as the heavens and earth do. He wants to free himself from obedience, or wants to deviate from the path of truth, which is straight and easy; therefore he collides with the laws of nature, and it is inevitable that these laws overpower him and shatter him to pieces. Then he returns and becomes obedient. Yes, those servants of Allah whose hearts, whose existence, whose movements, whose thoughts, whose will, whose desires and whose direction become harmonious with the laws of nature, such servants then bow in submission joyfully, and walking alongside this universe, they move with complete cooperation, and just as this whole universe moves in the direction of Allah, they too move flowing in that same direction. They do not fight the cosmic forces; when a believer reaches this stage, then miracles proceed from his hands, because he has united with the law of divine power. The great forces of this universe come to support him, and when this great power moves in the path of Allah, it moves in obedience.

If we obey Allah, we do so under compulsion. Would that we were obedient willingly! Would that we, like the heavens and earth, obeyed joyfully, with pleasure and delight, being in harmony with the spirit of the universe, and, with great joy, humility and reverence, moving towards Allah, the Lord of the worlds, saying labbayk and bowing in submission.

Sometimes ridiculous actions proceed from us. The chariot of destiny travels on its highway, swiftly; it travels on its direction; this whole universe travels with it, moving according to the constant laws of nature. We come and demand that we go ahead of destiny, or slow down from destiny, although we are part of this great universe. Because of our psychological weaknesses, when we separate from the caravan of the universe, our direction itself changes, and this direction changes because we become restless, hasty, greedy, self-interested and cowardly. We stray from the caravan of faith and the caravan of the universe; sometimes we collide this way, sometimes we roll that way and suffer pain, we fall here, we crash there, and we are shattered to pieces, while the chariot of the universe goes on its own path, at its fixed speed, towards its destined goal. In this way all our forces and all our struggles become futile. But when our hearts are filled with faith, when we bow in submission before Allah, when we are in harmony with the spirit of the universe, then we will know how genuine our role is. Then we will create balance between our steps and the pace of destiny, and we will move at the appropriate time, at the appropriate speed, in the appropriate direction. The power of this entire universe will join us, and we will be able to do great works in practice, except that we may be affected by pride and arrogance, because we would know the real truth: that the source of the power through which we are performing these outstanding deeds is in fact someone else. It is not our personal power. This blessing came into our power because it has been united with the power of Allah deposited within this universe.

What a blessing of felicity it would be, what contentment, what comfort and what tranquility, that we pass this brief journey on this earth, which answers the call of Allah, in joy, in the company of this earth, and finally arrive before the Lord, the Exalted, to begin a greater journey.

What a great peace and security it would be when we live in a universe which is our friend, all of which bows in submission before Allah, and we too are obedient to Allah. We both walk together, not in enmity, but as friends, because we are part of this universe and belong entirely to it.

﴿They said: "We come as obedient ones."﴾ (41:11)

﴿Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ (41:12)

﴿And revealed in each heaven its command﴾ (41:12). These two days may be those in which the stars were formed from sadam, or in which their formation was completed. Only Allah knows the reality. That the command of each heaven was revealed means that the laws of nature were enforced upon it, and it was guided to move in this manner. As for what the limits of the heaven are, we cannot determine that at present. One degree of distance could be one heaven; one galaxy could be one heaven; it is also possible that all the galaxies up to a certain distance are one heaven, or it could be otherwise. However, these heights are seven.

﴿And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made it well protected﴾ (41:12). The "nearest heaven" also has no fixed meaning; it may refer to the nearest galaxy, known among us as the Milky Way, whose diameter is one hundred thousand million light years. Or it may be some other standard to which, in Allah's sight, the word "sama" applies. In it are stars and stars, which are lamps for us, and very beautiful.

Protection from what? From devils. The Qur'an explicitly states this elsewhere. As for what the reality of the devils is, regarding the actions attributed to them in the Qur'an and the allusions to them, we can only say that the knowledge of their reality and nature belongs to Allah.

﴿That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ (41:12). This is the plan of a mighty and All-Knowing Being. Who besides Allah can run this great and terrifying universe? Only Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, can do this, He who is aware of everything.

After such a vast cosmic journey, what value remains for the position of those who deny, and what status remains for those who associate others with Allah, when the heavens and the earth together declare that they are obedient? But there is man, and what man? In relation to this universe, a very small ant, indeed a germ, worthless, crawling on the earth. He says with great heedlessness and arrogance: "I will not obey!" ... What punishment should be given to such people, such heedless arrogant ones!

Verses 9 to 12

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verses 13–18:

Verses 13 to 18

This is in truth a frightening warning.

Fa-in a'rada... wa Thamud (41:13): "Now if they turn away, say: I warn you of a sudden thunderbolt like the thunderbolt that struck ʿAd and Thamud." This warning was most fitting for the crimes and the most abhorrent immoralities of the polytheists, and for the arrogance in which the Makkan polytheists were immersed, which was mentioned at the beginning of the Surah. Moreover, they had also turned away from the path of obedience of this whole universe, which was mentioned immediately before this warning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 41, verse 21:

Here, suddenly, a scene comes before the readers: a scene of extreme distress. The authority of Allah is at its height. The limbs of a human being, by Allah's command, speak the word of truth. Whose limbs are these? The limbs of the enemies of Allah. What is the end of the enemies of Allah? They are gathered on the plain of Resurrection, from Adam (peace be upon him) down to the last human being born in this world, all present. They will be gathered like a herd. Then the enemies of God will be driven from among them. Where to? To the Fire, when the reckoning begins. Against them come witnesses whom they never expected. They see that their tongues are not supporting them, although these tongues used to lie in their favour, fabricate, and mock. Their ears, their eyes and their skins stand up against them in the court, and, with submission and acceptance, they bear witness before Allah, relating in full everything they had said. These people used to conceal all these things from Allah, and they thought that Allah was not seeing them. They consider their intentions and crimes to be minor, and they hide them; but they could not hide them from their own limbs. The limbs were with them; they were part of them. These limbs reveal the matters which they thought were secret mysteries hidden from all people. They are hidden even from the Lord of the worlds. This scene of the sovereignty and supreme authority of Allah suddenly comes before us. And the authority of Allah takes even our limbs away from us.

﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?"﴾ (41:21): they tell them the reality that was hidden from them, and they state this without any hesitation or reservation.

﴿They will say, "We have been made to speak by Allah who made everything speak; and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned."﴾ (41:21): Is it not He who gave speech to tongues? Can He not give speech to other limbs? Today He has made everything speak; now everything speaks.

﴿And He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned﴾ (41:21): The creation is also His, and eventually the return is also to Him. Nothing is beyond His power, and nothing can escape, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

They had denied these matters; now their own limbs confirm them. The next verse may be the narration of the speech of the limbs, and it may also be a commentary on this whole event.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verse 22:

﴿And you did not used to conceal yourselves [from being witnessed] ... nor your skins﴾ (41:22). "When you committed crimes in the world and hid yourselves, you did not have the thought that one day your own ears, your eyes and the skins of your bodies would testify against you." It did not even occur to you in imagination that these organs would rebel against you. Nor was it within your power to conceal yourselves from Allah in any way, even if you had wished to.

﴿But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do﴾ (41:22). "Rather, you thought that Allah was not aware of many of your deeds." Ignorance deceived you. This was a most foolish and wicked way of behaving, and it brought you to the brink of Hell.

This is Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 41, verse 23:

"And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers." (41:23)

And now, a comment on this entire scene and the lesson derived from it:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verse 24:

﴿فَإِن يَصْبِرُوا فَالنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَّهُمْ﴾ (41:24) "In such a state, if they endure patiently, the Fire is their abode." What a sober irony! Patience now is for the Fire of Jahannam. This is not the patience which brings a person joy and a good reward. It is the thing for which the recompense is the Fire of Jahannam, because it has now been decided that this is their abode.

﴿وَإِن يَسْتَعْتِبُوا فَمَا هُم مِّنَ الْمُعْتَبِينَ﴾ (41:24) "If they seek to be granted the opportunity to make amends, no opportunity will be given to them." There is neither approval there, nor any room for repentance. For one who seeks forgiveness, forgiveness is granted only when he seeks it after removing the wrong and injustice. Today the door of forgiveness and of setting things right has already been closed, and therefore they have no opportunity.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verse 25:

Now the next verse shows that the authority of Allah is established over your hearts as well. When you were on the earth, your hearts were still in the power of Allah even when you were disobeying Him. When Allah knew the inclination of your hearts toward corruption, He imposed upon your hearts companions from among the jinn and from among mankind. They would adorn evil for your minds and hearts. These companions would join them to the caravan whose end had been written as loss. Thus the word of punishment and the decree of punishment came true upon them:

Just see how far they are under the control of Allah, whose worship they consider beneath themselves. And their hearts, which lie in their sides, are leading them toward punishment and an evil end. Upon whomever Allah wishes to lead astray, He imposes companions who whisper suggestions into his heart, adorn for him whatever evil exists in his surroundings, and make his deeds appear good in his eyes, so that he sees no fault in them. The greatest sickness for a human being is that his awareness of his evil conduct and of his own misguidance disappears. When he comes to view every aspect of his self as good, then he draws close to destruction. For this reason, these people joined the group that was destined for destruction, that is, among those communities upon whom Allah's decree had already been settled, from among the jinn and from among mankind, that:

﴿Indeed, they were among the losers﴾ (41:25), "Surely they will remain in loss."

For the sake of misguiding those who were their companions, they urged them to confront the Qur'an in this way: do not listen to it, and do not let others listen to it, because they had found out that it has a powerful influence.

This is what the leaders (kubara') of Quraysh used to say to themselves and to the common people. These people had become powerless before the astonishing effectiveness of the Qur'an. Its influence was felt both upon them and upon the common folk.

﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an﴾ (41:26), because, as they used to say, it casts a spell upon them. It overpowers their thinking and is ruining their lives. It creates a rift between father and son, and separates husband and wife. There is no doubt that the Qur'an did create such separations, but this was because God Himself had created a separation between faith and disbelief, between guidance and misguidance. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verse 33:

The lesson concludes with the qualities and encouragement of a caller (da'i). It speaks of the spirit of his call, his words, his manners and his gentle, sweet manner of speech. These matters are directed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to all the callers of his Ummah. The surah began with the theme of how cruelly ordinary people treat the prophets and the callers, and how much insolence and arrogance they display. Therefore, here the caller is told: this is the method of your da'wah.

The work of Islamic da'wah is a very great and arduous task. The caller faces the complex psychology of the one addressed, his ignorance, his self-respect, his arrogance, his desires, his interests and his station and status. Calling to the sole sovereignty of Allah alone puts most of these things at risk. Then, to call in a class-based society that all people are equal to one another, and to take up the responsibility of da'wah in such circumstances, is in truth a very difficult task. But alongside being difficult, it is also a great task.

﴿And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah, does righteous work, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ (41:33). Those who have risen to carry the work of Islamic da'wah have the most exalted call in this world. Their words rise to the heavens as pure words. But along with the call, the caller's deeds must also be of this same kind. He must be one who bows in submission before Allah. His self should be lost in this call, all his works should become da'wah, and nothing of his own should remain in all his activities.

After this, the caller no longer cares what the reaction to his call is. Some deny, some are insolent, some are arrogant; in any case, the caller always proceeds with a good manner. He stands on a lofty station. His opponent brings evil. His opponent stands on an extremely low station.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 41, verse 34:

﴿Wa la tastawi al-hasanatu wa la as-sayyi'ah﴾ (41:34): "O Prophet, good and evil are not equal." It is not permissible for him to answer evil with evil. The effect of good and evil is not the same, nor is the worth of the two alike. The caller (dā'ī) should abandon the inner inclination to meet evil with evil, and should repel evil with patience, forgiveness and seriousness. He should bring harsh souls to trust and gentleness, so that enmity turns into friendship and harshness turns into softness.

﴿Idfa' billatī hiya aḥsan... ka-annahu waliyyun ḥamīm﴾ (41:34): "Repel evil with what is best, and you will see that the one who had enmity with you has become a close friend." This principle of Islam sometimes produces very good results. Many times it happens that fierce enmity turns into friendship, and anger and rancour cool down. Arrogance turns into modesty, provided that the one doing good knows how to speak well, can speak with seriousness, and can meet a highly agitated state with a smile, and can show a very cool temperament in the face of a person who has gone beyond himself.

If one confronts such a person in the same manner as he behaves, then what will happen? He will become even more beside himself, will act arrogantly and be inclined to rebellion, will cast off the garment of modesty and shame, and, beside himself, will be ready for war.

However, there is one condition: the person who displays such nobility must be a master of a great heart and a great station, and must be in a position where, if he wishes to answer a brick with a stone, he is able to do so. If there is the capacity to answer evil, then the effect of nobility will be felt. Otherwise, "the beggar's humility is the sign of his base nature." Let it not happen that adopting good conduct is regarded as weakness. If the opponent concludes that this person is weak, then he will certainly not show respect, and then goodness will have no effect.

Furthermore, it must also be noted that this nobility should be displayed on occasions of personal aggression. If someone attacks Islam and the principles of Allah, or inflicts oppression upon the believers, or prevents people from the religion, then in that case confrontation with every kind of weapon is necessary, or else, if there is no possibility of confrontation, patience may be observed. Let it not be that one is uprooting Islam while another is repaying evil with good.

This station, of repelling evil with good, and of showing tolerance and forbearance at the place of anger and wrath, and of being able to decide where tolerance and forbearance are to be shown and where evil is to be repelled with good, is a great rank. Not every person can attain this rank. Only one who has been given a great measure of patience can be established in this station. It is the station upon which only the special servants of Allah and those who are patient can be established.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verse 36:

﴿Wa immā yanzaghannaka min al-shaytāni nazghun fa-ista'idh billāh; innahu huwa al-samī' al-'alīm﴾ (41:36) "And if an incitement from Satan should reach you, seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

In anger there is sometimes an incitement toward revenge. Because of evil, a person at times feels a lack of patience, or feels constriction of heart in matters of nobility. In such circumstances one should recite: a'ūdhu billāhi min al-shayṭāni al-rajīm (I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed). By this, the breach that Satan intended to make is closed.

Allah is the Creator of the human heart; He is well acquainted with its ups and downs. He also knows its strength and its limit of endurance. He knows through which opening Satan attacks: he encircles the heart of the caller (dā'ī) and incites it. It is Allah alone who is the Protector. Because this path is difficult, this way is very arduous. The caller has to travel through the ups and downs of the human soul and the intricate valleys of the human self, so that the caller may fulfil the right of guidance and leadership in its deep psychological inclinations.

Lesson No. 228 — At a Glance

This lesson is also connected with the Islamic call. It begins with the cosmic signs and presents the alternation of night and day for our reflection, and it presents the sun and moon because among the polytheists there were some who worshipped the sun and the moon, although both are among the creations of God. Despite these verses, these people deny the signs of God and do not worship Him; yet with God there is a creation that is constantly engaged in His worship. Then this entire earth also is engaged in the worship of God: it becomes dead and then receives the life-giving bounty from God, just as God has also given life to man, yet man disobeys. He gives the signs of God a perverse meaning; he distorts the meanings of the verses of the Qur'an, although the Glorious Qur'an is in clear Arabic. After this, one of the scenes of the Resurrection comes before us. Then, by presenting his own life, it is shown that man is a weak creature, greedy for wealth, and when some difficulty befalls him he laments and wails. And at the end of the surah, attention is drawn to the arguments and signs of the self and the horizons, so that the truth becomes manifest to the people and the doubts in their hearts are removed.

The signs to which these verses point are spread out before our eyes; the learned can see them and so can the unlearned, and they have direct and profound effects upon the human heart, even if a person does not know their scientific reality at all, because between man and this universe there exists a connection deeper than scientific knowledge. Both were created by God; their nature is one, their structure is one. Man is a part of this universe, and this universe is also a part of man. The substance of their existence is one, their nature is one, and the law of nature according to which man moves is the same according to which this universe moves. Both have one Deity. Therefore man possesses a profound feeling and a deep natural perception concerning these heavens and earth, and this perception is attained through a deep natural logic.

For this reason the Qur'an Karim suffices only with directing man's attention to it, and awakening him from heedlessness. This heedlessness falls upon people because, having kept seeing the alternation of night and day and the sun and moon, they no longer hold any importance for them. Veils have come over their hearts and minds, so the Qur'an awakens man and polishes his thinking, saying: reflect a little upon these marvels; these are parts of your familiar universe; you live with night and day and with the sun and moon.

Attention was also drawn, in connection with the sun and moon, to a deviation and an intellectual aberration. Some people used to worship the sun and moon so that through this they might attain nearness to God, since prostrating before the best of God's creation is considered prostrating before God. The Qur'an, here, has definitively corrected this deviation and has also cleansed the pollution of beliefs. If you truly worship God, then do not worship the sun and moon,

﴿But prostrate to God, who created them﴾ (41:37). Creation should turn only to the Creator, and the sun and moon, like you, are followers of God alone. God created these two, the sun and the moon, and for these two He has used the feminine plural pronoun here, because the reference here is to the genus of stars and planets, not merely these two. And the feminine plural form of rational beings is used for them in their predicate because they too are, like you, persons who worship God.

After these signs and proofs and this proclamation and explanation, if they still act arrogantly, this does not cause any increase or decrease in God's dominion, nor any advance or delay; with God there are countless creatures engaged in His worship.

This passage is the commentary on verse 38 of Surah Fussilat (41), so I'll translate it as it stands.

The closest and most apparent meaning is that by "those who are with your Lord" is meant the angels. However, some other creation composed of the righteous servants of Allah may also be intended by it. We know very little about the creations of Allah.

Those who are with the Lord are a exalted and high creation; they are more honoured and exemplary people. They do not show arrogance before Allah in the way that this weak creature of the earth, man, does, nor are they afflicted with the delusion that "we are the close ones of Allah." And at no time of the night or day do they stop or grow weary of glorifying Allah.

﴿وَهُمْ لَا يَسْأَمُونَ﴾ (41:38) "and they never tire." Therefore, even if all of the people of the (heavenly) assembly were to abandon the worship of Allah, it would make no difference to the worship of Allah.

Just look at this earth in which they live, from which they are born, and into which they will be returned and buried. This earth, upon which they crawl like ants, has no source of food and drink for them anywhere except this earth. This earth too stands before Allah in utmost humility and awe. When it becomes dead, it is Allah alone who gives it life and makes it green and flourishing.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 41, verse 39:

The manner in which the Qur'an expresses itself is worth noting in every place. The earth being "in a state of khushu'" (humility/stillness) means that before the rain it was dormant and in a dead condition. When the rain fell, it stirred, became green and fresh, as though it gave thanks and fell prostrate, for it had received life. In the context where this example comes, the theme being discussed is worship, humility and submission, praise and glorification. Accordingly, the earth is shown in such a state as though it too is alive and, in relation to Allah, it too possesses awareness. It is appropriate that I quote here a page from my own book al-Taswir al-Fanni fi al-Quran:

"The Qur'an has described the condition of the earth before rain, in some places as khashi'ah (dormant, dead and awed) and in some places as hamidah (dry, extinguished, dead). Some people think this is merely variety of expression, but we must see in which context each of the two words is used and how. The Qur'an has used these words in two different contexts:

The word hamidah has come in Surah al-Hajj:

"O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then know that We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then [We develop you] that you may reach your maturity. And among you is one who is taken in death, and among you is one who is returned to the feeblest age, so that he knows nothing after knowing. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it stirs and swells and grows every beautiful kind of plant." (22:5)

And the word khashi'ah has come in this context:

"And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship. But if they are arrogant, then those with your Lord [the angels] glorify Him by night and by day, and they never tire. And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells." (41:37-39)

A brief glance at these two contexts makes the connection between hamidah and khashi'ah evident. In the first context the theme is raising, giving life and bringing forth. Therefore, the state of the earth as dead (hamidah) is more appropriate with it. After deadness it comes into motion, swells, and produces pairs of every beautiful kind of vegetation (here I would say the word zawj is also highly meaningful). In the second context the theme is worship, submission and humility, so with it the image of the earth as khashi'ah and awed is more appropriate. And when rain falls, it swells up.

Here, in this second context, after the earth stirs and swells, there is no mention of plants growing, whereas in the first context there is mention, because here the theme is worship, and growing plants have no connection with worship. The words ihtazzat wa rabat (41:39) also have two different purposes in the two places. Here, in the second context, the meaning is that the earth came into motion, just as all moving things in that scene come into motion for worship. Therefore the earth should not be left in a state of humility and deadness. So here it stirred so that it might join the other worshippers in worship, and all the parts of the scene might be included in it. Thus the expression takes into account the very fine details of the harmony of its composition, whereas in the first context ihtazzat wa rabat (41:39) is for the motion of the act of creation."

Now we return again to the flow of the discussion: from the argument of the revival of this same earth, the conclusion that in the same way Allah will bring forth the dead on the Day of Resurrection.

"Indeed, He who revived it is the one who will surely bring the dead to life; indeed, He is over all things competent." (41:39) Through scenes of this kind the Qur'an repeatedly argues that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will raise the dead in the same way, and from such scenes the Qur'an also repeatedly argues for Allah's boundless power. Man observes very closely the scenes of vegetative and other life within the earth. Before reason, these variegated forms affect the heart. When life emerges from death, a person watches this miracle of power with great wonder, and its effects settle into human consciousness; and the Qur'an's manner is that it addresses the natural consciousness rather than reason alone.

Now, after such detailed explanation and cosmic evidence and proofs, if people give these signs a perverted meaning or commit distortion (ilhad) in the verses of the Quran, then let them prepare for their own end. These people deny the clear verses of Allah and cast confusion into them.

This threat, although indirect and general, is extremely dangerous.

Lā yakhfawna ʿalaynā (41:40): "They are not hidden from Us." Before Allah's knowledge they are entirely in plain view. Therefore those who commit ilhad, who give the meanings of the Quran a perverted sense, will be punished for it, even if they create confusions and interpretations, even if they think that they will escape from the hands of Allah. Just as they create confusions and interpretations in the meanings of the Quran, even if they think that they will escape from the hands of Allah, and just as they, by casting confusion into the meanings of the Quran, free themselves from their responsibilities, or make it a pretext before the people.

After this general warning, a somewhat more explicit statement follows:

Afaman yulqā ... yawm al-qiyāmah (41:40): "Then is he who is cast into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?" This is the explicit statement of the threat: being thrown into the Fire and wailing await you, whereas the believers will come with complete peace and tranquility.

In this verse there is another threat as well:

Iʿmalū mā shi'tum innahu bimā taʿmalūna baṣīr (41:40): "Do whatever you wish; indeed He sees all that you do." How wretched is the person who is left free to do whatever he pleases. He may create confusion in the signs of Allah as he likes, while Allah is recording all his deeds.

Now the current context moves on to those who reject the Qur'an, even though it is a mighty and dominant Book, and is extremely well protected. Falsehood cannot even draw near to it.

The verse speaks of those who deny the Reminder of their Lord when it has come to them. But it does not mention who these people are or what their end will be. It is a subject (mubtada') without a predicate (khabar). This means that their deed is so abominable that there are no words to describe it. They are committing a very evil act. Instead of giving a report about these people, the details are given of what kind of reminder and admonition it is that they are denying, so that the repugnance of their action may be understood even more.

﴿Indeed, it is a mighty Book.﴾ (41:41) ﴿Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One who is Wise and Praiseworthy.﴾ (41:42) How can falsehood enter this Book? It has been sent down by Allah, the Truth, who makes the truth clear, and this Book is connected to the truth upon which the heavens and the earth [are founded]... This Book is a mighty Book, it is protected, and Allah has taken upon Himself the responsibility of its protection.

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian.﴾ (15:9)

Whoever contemplates the Qur'an attains the truth with which it was revealed. It was revealed so that it might be recited, and whoever recites it will find this truth on one side in his soul, and on the other side in its texts. Every person can derive the truth from the Qur'an with great simplicity and ease. This truth is extremely natural, satisfying, and present within human nature. The Book has a very deep and wonderful effect on every reader.

And then this Book.

"A revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy" (41:42). Wisdom is hidden in its very composition; its manner of revelation and its guidance make wisdom manifest. Therefore the Lord who has sent it down deserves abundant praise. This is why the Qur'an repeatedly urges praise and glorification.

Now the Qur'an is linked with the earlier scriptures. A bond is established between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and all the earlier prophets, so that they form one assembly, one family; their message is one, their spirit and heart are one, and their method of calling to the truth is also one. Thus every Muslim feels that he is a leaf of a tree with countless leaves, whose roots are deep, and that he is a member of an assembly that begins with Adam (peace be upon him):

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verse 43:

ما يقال لك ۔۔۔۔۔ وذوا عقاب اليم (41:43) "O Prophet (ﷺ), nothing is being said to you that was not already said to the messengers before you. Indeed your Lord is Most Forgiving, and also Possessor of a painful punishment."

There is one revelation, one messengership, one creed, and throughout history humanity has had one and the same response to it. All peoples denied, and all raised the same objection. Therefore there is a single firm bond among all the prophets: one lineage, one family, one pain and one hardship. Their experiences are alike, their aims are alike, their path is one, and their method is one.

What a deep awareness of affection and love this is! An awareness of strength, patience and profound steadfastness. The caller (to Islam) is being given the indication that you are travelling on a path on which Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ) travelled before you. What an awareness of honour and elevation is being conveyed: endure the hardships of this path, its stumbling blocks, its thorns and difficulties, for this path belongs to great people. It is the path of the prophets and the righteous, and with this awareness the caller's capacity for endurance increases.

And this is a reality.

ما يقال لك إلا ما قد قيل للرسل من قبلك (41:43) "Nothing is being said to you that was not already said to the messengers before you." Though this may seem a simple matter, the great effects of fixing this truth in the hearts and minds of the believers cannot be measured. Only the Qur'an can accomplish this. It plants the seeds of this great truth in hearts, and from God, the messengers and Muhammad (ﷺ) were told:

إن ربك لذو مغفرة وذو عقاب أليم (41:43) "Indeed your Lord is Most Forgiving, and also Possessor of a painful punishment." Forgiveness is accompanied by punishment so that balance may be established. A person who hopes for forgiveness should also fear the painful punishment; he should neither despair nor become fearless. The truth is that balance is a fundamental principle of Islamic teaching.

After this it is said that it is God's mercy that He revealed the Qur'an in clear Arabic, in your own language; yet your obstinacy, your confusions, your disputation, and then the distortions in that Book, are cause for wonder.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 41, verse 44:

"If We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, 'Why have its verses not been explained in detail? What a strange thing: a non-Arabic discourse addressed to an Arab!'" (41:44). These people do not lend their ears to an Arabic Qur'an, because they fear its overwhelming influence. It is an Arabic discourse that addresses the innate nature of the Arabs, it is in their own language, and yet they say: do not listen to this Qur'an, and create confusion in it. When it is recited, make an uproar; in this way you will prevail. Now, if it were non-Arabic, they would still object, asking why the Qur'an was not revealed in Arabic, why it was not expressed in a detailed and eloquent language. And if part of it were Arabic and part non-Arabic, they would say, "Then why is it partly Arabic and partly non-Arabic?" In short, their aim in every case is to raise objections.

From this argument and dispute the reality that emerges is that this quarrel is only about words and language, and not about the teachings of the Qur'an. In terms of its teachings, it is guidance and healing for the believers. It is the hearts of the believers that grasp its reality, and therefore they receive guidance and healing from it. As for those who do not believe, their hearts are blind; the light of the Qur'an does not reach them. There is a plug in their ears. They are blind of heart, and therefore they find nothing in this Book. Why? Because these people are very far from the temperament of this Book; they do not understand its voice.

"Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing; but for those who do not believe, it is a plug in their ears and a covering over their eyes. They are like those who are being called from a far-off place" (41:44). The application of this verse extends to people of every time, every place and every society. Some people are such that this Qur'an works upon their souls and transforms them into something entirely different; it brings the dead to life, and they become great people in their own selves and in their environment. Others are such that this Qur'an weighs heavily upon their hearts and minds, and when it is recited to them, it makes them even more blind and deaf. The Qur'an is the same; the difference lies in the hearts.

The message of Muhammad (ﷺ) declared that humanity had now come of age, and the burden of freedom was placed upon its shoulders. Every person has been made personally responsible for their own deeds. Now, whoever wishes may take whichever path they choose.

﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ (41:46).

The earlier verses referred to the Hour, and in them there was also an allusion to God dealing justly with everyone, so that no one will be wronged. For this reason it is also said here that knowledge of the Hour belongs to God alone. In this connection, a picture of God's knowledge is also drawn, showing how profound and detailed His knowledge is in every matter, and some examples are given. After this, a scene of the Hereafter is presented, in which the polytheists are questioned and respond.

The Hour is an unseen matter, hidden in the unknown and in the womb of the future. Likewise, of the blossoms, the fruits that will emerge in the future are known to God alone. Likewise, the pregnancy in the womb is also unseen, hidden from view. All of these are within God's knowledge. Human thought runs after the fruits that emerge from flowers and buds, after the children in the wombs of mothers; our thought runs through the rises and falls of this vast earth and reflects upon countless flowers and blossoms. Then there are the children in the womb of every female, whose number it is not within human power to determine, the habits of all humans and animals, and the females of beasts, birds and insects. The truth is that the steed of human imagination tires and falls down again and again. The very notion of the limits of God's knowledge is not conceivable, for it is unbounded.

From among humans, a small flock of the misguided will one day confront this knowledge, and nothing will be outside the circle of that knowledge.

﴿And on the day when He will call to them, "Where are My partners?"﴾ (41:47). Then no dispute, argument or deception will be of any use, nor will any twisting or distortion of words be able to pass; what then could they say, other than:

﴿They will say, "We have informed You that none of us is a witness to it today."﴾ (41:47). They will say, "We have already made our declaration: none of us today is a witness to this." O God, we have indeed informed You that today none of us is a witness to this matter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 41, verse 48:

وضل عنهم ما ۔۔۔۔۔ من محيص (41:48) "Those whom they used to invoke before will vanish from them, and they will realize that there is no place of refuge for them."

Because at that time they will have no knowledge of their former claim so that they could confirm it. The conviction will have settled deeply in their souls that there is now no place of escape. This will be their anguished and stupefying state on that day. When such a state comes upon a person, he forgets his entire past, and then he remembers only the circumstances that confront him.

This is how dreadful that Day is, yet man is utterly careless about it. Man is extremely greedy for every kind of good, but he does not take the slightest thought for the good of the Hereafter. Man begins to wail and lament over a trivial calamity, yet he gives no thought to the terrifying wailing and lamentation of the Day of Resurrection. Here the inner image of the human soul is drawn. All clothing and coverings are stripped away, and by removing every kind of gilding and embellishment, the true colour of the human form is shown.

This is a most truthful portrait of the human soul. Even its extremely fine features have been brought into clear view. Those who do not believe in the guidance of Allah, and those who do believe, are on a perfectly straight path, and they have one and the same manner and outlook. But the psychology of the misguided people is this: they change suddenly, are weak of will, are enamoured of show, are greedy for wealth, are ungrateful, are proud in prosperity and wail and lament in adversity. In short, this is a very detailed portrait of these people, and a strange portrait it is.

Man never tires of asking for good. He prays for good with great insistence and entreaty, and never tires of making such supplication. But if evil merely touches him in passing, he loses all hope and becomes utterly despairing. He thinks that there is no hope of escaping or being saved from this evil. Thus he concludes that all means and resources have come to an end. His chest becomes constricted, and he becomes sorrowful and anxious. He despairs of the mercies and kindnesses of Allah. This is because he has no trust in his Lord, and his bond with his Lord is weak.

But this same man, when Allah bestows upon him His mercies and kindnesses and the calamity departs, then the blessings of Allah ... and make him arrogant. He does not give thanks. Now prosperity lifts him up to the heavens. He says, "This is my due. I deserve it by my own ability, and this is my right." This person forgets the Hereafter and regards it as beyond possibility. He says:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 41, verses 50–51:

"وما اظن الساعة قائمة" (41:50): "I do not think the Hour will ever come." Now this person is intoxicated with himself. He puts Allah under an obligation, and he imagines that with Allah too his status will be the same as it is here, whereas he will have no status at all. He is a denier and a disbeliever in the Hereafter. Despite this, he thinks that if he goes to Allah, he will still be counted among the honourable people there.

"ولئن رجعت الى ربي ان لي عنده للحسنى" (41:50): "And even if I am indeed returned to my Lord, I will surely have a good time there too." This is baseless arrogance. Now comes a most fitting warning.

"فلننبئن الذين ... عذاب غليظ" (41:50): "Surely We will inform those who disbelieve of what they have done, and We will make them taste a harsh punishment." This is man: when Allah makes him prosperous, he becomes rebellious, turns away and becomes arrogant. But if harm reaches him, then he collapses. He considers himself humiliated and wretched, becomes helpless and weak, begins to wail and moan, and makes lengthy supplications.

Just look: how precisely the Qur'an has recorded the small and large actions and reactions of the human psyche. This is the word of Allah, who is the Creator of man, and the Creator himself is telling us that this is Man. For the Creator knows well every part of His creation. Allah knows that man keeps wandering through these ups and downs, unless he is taken hold of and led to the Straight Path. Only then does he walk upon the right way.

After this most unveiled picture of the human self, Allah asks them: what will you do at that time, you who deny the Book? If it is indeed from Allah, and you become deserving of the punishment with which you are being warned, and at that time you bring upon yourselves the consequences of denial and enmity.
